one_liner: Grisu3-based double<->string library extracted from V8; beats sprintf/ostringstream, covers both to_chars- and from_chars-like directions.
what_it_does: Provides DoubleToStringConverter (ToShortest/ToFixed/ToExponential/ToPrecision) and StringToDoubleConverter (StringToDouble/StringToFloat) for IEEE-double formatting and parsing. Not a drop-in for sprintf/ostringstream: callers construct a configured converter object, pass flags (e.g. EMIT_POSITIVE_EXPONENT_SIGN, ALLOW_HEX), and write into a caller-provided StringBuilder wrapping a fixed char buffer. Code was extracted and refactored out of V8's own number-conversion routines for standalone reuse.
how_it_is_fast: Formatting uses the Grisu3 algorithm (fast-dtoa.cc): 64-bit fixed-precision 'DiyFp' arithmetic plus precomputed cached powers of ten (cached-powers.cc) generate the shortest round-trippable decimal directly, skipping printf format-string parsing and avoiding arbitrary-precision math for the common case. When Grisu3 can't resolve a value unambiguously it falls back to an exact bignum algorithm (bignum-dtoa.cc). Parsing (strtod.cc) mirrors this: a DiyFp fast path handles typical inputs and only escalates to bignum arithmetic for correctly-rounded edge cases.
when_to_use: JSON/serialization code needing shortest round-trippable double<->string conversion at high throughput (already used inside V8, Chromium, RapidJSON)
Hot paths currently bottlenecked on sprintf/ostringstream for float formatting
Need both formatting and parsing directions from one small dependency instead of stitching together separate libraries
Targeting older/pre-C++11 toolchains (utils.h ships fallback macros for pre-C++11 compilation)
Cross-platform desktop/server build via scons/cmake/bazel; willing to link a small library rather than stay header-only
when_not_to_use: Need an actual drop-in for std::to_chars/std::from_chars call sites — API shape is a converter class with explicit buffers/flags, not a function-call replacement
Code relies on ToPrecision(): it can fall onto the slow bignum-fallback path for many inputs and become slower than sprintf (open issue #83, unresolved as of this research)
Inputs frequently have decimal expansions of the form N*10^M — same Grisu3-fails/bignum-fallback slow path (open issue #28, open since 2016, still open)
Need header-only, zero-build-step integration — this requires its own static/shared library build step (scons/cmake/bazel)
Parsing throughput is the priority — open issue #153 reports StringToDouble is slower than other dtoa-style parsers on some inputs; a parsing specialist may win there

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (also viable as a source-drop: 8 .cc files, no header-only mode)
integration.min_toolchain: no CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD is pinned; utils.h carries pre-C++11 fallback macros, so the code itself targets C++03+; CMake path requires CMake 3.29+, scons/bazel builds don't
integration.platforms: x86-64, arm64 (issue #6 confirms arm64 support), and other GCC/Clang/MSVC targets; no SIMD/ISA requirement
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; DoubleToStringConverter/StringToDoubleConverter hold only constructor-set config and write into caller-supplied buffers, so concurrent calls against one shared const converter instance look safe by design, but this is not asserted anywhere in the docs
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: functionally covers what std::to_chars/std::from_chars and sprintf/ostringstream do, but requires rewriting call sites to the converter-class API with explicit output buffers/StringBuilder

gotchas: ToShortest() needs a buffer sized to at least kBase10MaximalLength+1 (or kMaxCharsEcmaScriptShortest=25 for the EcmaScript preset) or the call can fail; buffer sizing is the caller's responsibility
ToPrecision() can silently take the slow bignum-fallback path and end up worse than sprintf for a large class of inputs (open issue #83)
DoubleToAscii on N*10^M-shaped values hits the same Grisu3-fails/bignum-fallback slow path (open issue #28, open since 2016)
ALLOW_HEX and ALLOW_OCTALS parsing flags only apply to integer literals; combining them with fractional/exponent characters yields 'trailing junk' rather than a parse error
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over milo Grisu2 (miloyip/dtoa-benchmark) when you want the battle-tested, actively maintained, V8-derived implementation with real production adoption (V8, Chromium, RapidJSON) rather than a single-header benchmark contender that happens to be faster in that one shootout. Pick c4core or fast_double_parser instead when raw throughput matters more than provenance: c4core's own README claims 40%-2x faster than std::to_chars, and fast_double_parser is a parsing-only specialist that issue #153 suggests may beat double-conversion's StringToDouble.
verified_claims_summary: On the independent miloyip/dtoa-benchmark RandomDigit workload (1,000 random doubles, 1-17 significant digits, shortest round-trippable ASCII, min of 10x100 trials), double-conversion's EcmaScriptConverter().ToShortest() averaged 201.645ns vs sprintf's 1256.376ns (6.23x) and std::ostringstream's 2,778.748ns (~13.8x, derived), on an Intel Core i7 920 @2.67GHz built with VC++2013 Win64 release config (only premake's {"Optimize"} flag is itemized, no literal compiler flags).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-13, enrolled in OSS-Fuzz and OpenSSF Scorecard) and BSD-3-Clause; not header-only, so it needs a small build step or manual vendoring of its ~8 .cc files, but has no external dependencies.
